blocks.content: A service's restart policy tells Docker what to do when its container exits, whether to leave it stopped, or bring it back automatically, and under exactly which conditions.

Compose supports the same restart policies plain docker run --restart does: no (the default, never restart automatically), always (restart no matter why it exited), on-failure (restart only if it exited with an error), and unless-stopped (restart automatically, except if you explicitly stopped it yourself).

blocks.alt: Four options, each with a distinct trigger condition

blocks.content: The distinction matters in practice: on-failure only restarts a container that exited with a non-zero (error) status, a clean, intentional exit is left alone. always is less discriminating, it restarts the container regardless of why it stopped, including a clean exit.

blocks.alt: Restart only on error, versus restart no matter what

blocks.content: This is the practical reason unless-stopped is often preferred over plain always in production: if you deliberately run docker compose stop, an unless-stopped service correctly stays down, an always service would restart itself right back up the next time the Docker daemon restarts, ignoring your explicit intent.

blocks.alt: A manual stop is respected, not silently overridden

blocks.content: For a genuinely long-running production service, unless-stopped (or always if you never intend to manually stop it) is the common choice, for a one-off task or a batch job meant to run once and exit, the default no is correct, you do not want it silently restarting in a loop.

blocks.alt: The right default depends on whether the service is meant to run forever

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: restart: no, always, on-failure, and unless-stopped give increasingly automatic recovery, each triggered under different exit conditions.
unless-stopped is usually the safer production default over always, since it respects a deliberate, manual stop instead of overriding it.
